items.followUp: What is the difference between an ordered list and an unordered list in HTML?

rubric.why: An ordered list presents items in a numbered or lettered sequence.
rubric.description: States how an ordered list displays its items.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that an ordered list uses numbers or letters.

rubric.why: An unordered list presents items without a numbered sequence, commonly using bullets.
rubric.description: States how an unordered list displays its items.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that an unordered list uses bullets or another non-sequential marker.

modelAnswer: An ordered list displays items in a numbered or lettered sequence.
An unordered list displays items with bullets or other markers, without a specific sequence.

rubric.description: Shows the correct hexadecimal place-value expansion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct expansion using the digits C=12, 9, 2, and 1.
Award 1 mark for the correct decimal result.

items.followUp: Write two differences between RAM and secondary storage.

rubric.why: Memory is generally temporary or volatile, while storage retains data for later use.
rubric.description: Gives the difference in how long data is retained.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that memory is temporary/volatile and storage is permanent/non-volatile.

rubric.why: Memory is faster and directly accessible to the CPU, unlike storage devices.
rubric.description: Gives a difference in speed or CPU access.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct comparison of speed or direct CPU access.

modelAnswer: Memory is usually temporary (volatile), while storage keeps data for long-term use (non-volatile).
Memory is faster and is directly accessed by the CPU; storage is generally slower.

items.followUp: Make a truth table for the AND operator.

rubric.description: Gives the correct output for input 0.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the row 0 → 1, or false → true.

rubric.description: Gives the correct output for input 1.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the row 1 → 0, or true → false.

rubric.why: A patent grants a legal or exclusive right to the inventor.
rubric.description: Identifies the patent as a legal or exclusive right.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the right granted by a patent.

rubric.why: The right concerns an invention and is granted to its inventor or owner.
rubric.description: Identifies what the patent protects and who receives the right.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning an invention and its inventor/owner.

modelAnswer: A patent is a legal right granted to an inventor or owner for an invention.
It gives the holder exclusive rights to make, use, or sell the invention for a specified period.

items.followUp: What is one way CAPTCHA helps protect a website?

rubric.why: CAPTCHA is used to distinguish human users from automated programs.
rubric.description: States that CAPTCHA checks whether a user is human.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that CAPTCHA distinguishes people from bots.

rubric.why: This helps prevent automated abuse such as spam or fake submissions.
rubric.description: States a website abuse CAPTCHA can help prevent.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning bots, spam, or another automated misuse.

modelAnswer: CAPTCHA helps a website distinguish human users from automated programs (bots).
It helps prevent automated activities such as spam, fake account creation, or false form submissions.

items.followUp: Name the two main categories of transmission media and give one example of each.

rubric.why: Guided media carry signals through a physical path, such as a cable.
rubric.description: Names the guided or wired category.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming guided/wired transmission media.

rubric.why: Unguided media carry signals through air or space without a physical cable.
rubric.description: Names the unguided or wireless category.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming unguided/wireless transmission media.

modelAnswer: Transmission media are of two main types: guided (wired) and unguided (wireless).
Guided examples include twisted-pair cable, coaxial cable, and fibre-optic cable; unguided examples include radio waves, microwaves, and infrared.

items.followUp: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage of a dynamic IP address.

rubric.why: A static IP address is assigned as a fixed address and normally remains unchanged.
rubric.description: Describes the fixed nature of a static IP address.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a static address is fixed or does not normally change.

rubric.why: A dynamic IP address is assigned automatically, usually by DHCP, and may change over time.
rubric.description: Describes how a dynamic IP address is assigned or that it can change.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a dynamic address is assigned automatically or may change.

modelAnswer: A static IP address is manually assigned and normally remains the same.
A dynamic IP address is assigned automatically, usually by DHCP, and may change over time.
